name: ADR Directive
impact_assessment: SEC(2011) 1408 (joint with the ODR Regulation; executive summary SEC(2011) 1409)
evidence_rating: thin: Commission application report (2019) and evaluation (2023) based on administrative data, surveys and consultation
summary: By 2019 consumers had access to certified dispute-resolution bodies in virtually all retail sectors, but the Commission found the system under-used: low awareness among consumers and low participation by traders. Its 2023 evaluation, annexed to the impact assessment for the amending proposal, confirmed this and led to targeted amendments.

indicators.objective: No monitoring indicators set in the proposal; assessed through the Commission's reports listed below
Consumers can use ADR for disputes with traders
indicators.indicator: ADR coverage, awareness and trader participation
indicators.evidence: 2019: full sector coverage reached; framework 'underused'; ODR platform led to direct settlement in up to 42% of cases. 2023: low trader participation remains the main obstacle.

literature.citation: European Commission (2019), Report on the application of Directive 2013/11/EU on alternative dispute resolution for consumer disputes and Regulation (EU) No 524/2013 on online dispute resolution, COM(2019) 425
literature.title: Report on the application of Directive 2013/11/EU on alternative dispute resolution for consumer disputes and Regulation (EU) No 524/2013 on online dispute resolution
literature.headline: High-quality ADR available in virtually all retail sectors; the framework is underused because of low awareness, complex national landscapes and low trader uptake
literature.summary_plain: Out-of-court dispute bodies now exist for almost every kind of purchase, but few consumers and traders use them.

literature.citation: European Commission (2023), Impact Assessment accompanying the proposal amending Directive 2013/11/EU on alternative dispute resolution (evaluation of the ADR Directive annexed), SWD(2023) 335
literature.title: Impact Assessment accompanying the proposal amending Directive 2013/11/EU on alternative dispute resolution (evaluation of the ADR Directive annexed)
literature.headline: Evaluation confirms low participation by traders as the main obstacle; disparities between Member States in ADR use persist
literature.summary_plain: The Commission's evaluation confirmed that the rules work where traders take part, but that many traders do not.
